resources.string: At your saved home (mock on; tap \"Stop\" to return to your real location)

A patrol starts from your "current real GPS location" by default (the homes saved here are only destinations for "Go home"). It only teleports the one time you tap "Teleport" yourself; automatic returns and the notification's "Go home" always walk.

You can save several homes here (Home 1, Home 2…). When you tap "Go home", you can "Walk" or "Teleport" to each destination: your real location (ends the mock) or one of your homes (stays there with the mock on; tap "Stop" to return to your real location).

Tap a saved home to center it on the map or delete it.
Move the map so the crosshair is on your home
Walk back to real location (mock ends on arrival)
Teleport back to real location (mock ends now)
Walk to %1$s (stay there, mock stays on)
Teleport to %1$s (stay there, mock stays on)
Stopping ends the mock location, and the game will jump from your saved home straight back to your real GPS location. Stop now?
On the way home. If you stop now, the game will jump from the current position straight back to your real GPS location.
The game already sees your real location, so stopping won\'t cause another jump. The virtual location and this patrol\'s progress will end.
The patrol is still starting. If you stop now, the mock won\'t start.
Back at your saved home; mock location still on

In bird\'s-eye view: pause patrol → tap the Big Flower → tap its name label → swipe down on the info page → close → walk on. Each step checks with screen capture that the screen changed before doing the next. Needs a scan (screen capture) running, and the \"Pikmin Bloom GPS: Auto Nectar\" accessibility service turned on in system settings. Note: any app can see which accessibility services are on, so the game could use this to detect it. Only turn it on when you need it.
Turn on \"Pikmin Bloom GPS: Auto Nectar\" in Accessibility settings
%1$s: tapped the flower and swiped to collect

A vehicle goes to the \"next\" Big Flower at its own speed and switches back to walking on arrival. Above about 20 km/h the game doesn\'t plant flowers and no steps are written, so it\'s handy for rushing to a mushroom or moving to another area.
Joystick on: up = north. When you turn it off, the route continues from where you are
Joystick off; back on the route
Start a patrol first for the joystick to work
The joystick is on the floating bar. Turn on the floating bar first
Hold and drag to move the joystick
Cruise control: keeps walking in the last direction even after you let go of the joystick. Tap it again, or \"Go home\", \"Stop\" or \"Go now\" to stop
Push the joystick in a direction first, then tap the lock
Route updated; continuing from your current position
Start from real location, go and stay there
Heading to %1$s; will stay on arrival
The patrol is paused next to this flower. After collecting your rewards, tap \"Resume\" to continue the patrol.
Arrived at %1$s, staying here (tap \"Resume\" to continue the patrol)
Real location: every app on the phone sees the real GPS, and the virtual patrol waits for you. Tap \"Back to virtual location…\" to jump back
Switched to real location: all apps (including the game) see the real GPS. Tap the location button again to go back
Switched to real location. The virtual patrol waits where it was; to go back, tap \"Back to virtual location…\"
Switched back to virtual location; the patrol picks up where it left off
Real location: the scan continues after you tap \"Back to virtual location…\"
Ask to switch to real location when Google Maps opens

When Google Maps comes to the front, a small window asks you (tap outside it or tap \"No thanks\" to do nothing). Only tapping \"Switch to real location\" removes the mock location (the patrol state is kept), and at that moment the game sees your real location too; to go back, you always have to tap \"Back to virtual location…\" yourself. No need to switch just to look up a shop or read reviews. Needs \"Usage access\"; without the \"Display over other apps\" permission, it asks with a notification instead.
